applies_why: Yes: the judge resolves the Isaiah 7:14 issue by separating the challenger's wording answer from the defender's application answer rather than weighing the two chains together by footing.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — reading one: the judge must assess the whole pressed chain and answering chain together by their footings; reading two: the judge may find underdetermined merely because one side addressed wording and the other application.
why: The judge's reason splits the Isaiah 7:14 dispute into wording versus application and does not weigh the two sides' chains together by footing as K-C requires.
